summary: Order in Petition No. 130/MP/2026 - _(b) Issue appropriate and consequential directions to the Respondent(s) to give effect to the phased commissioning permitted by this Hon’ble Commission in a time-bound manner;_ - _(c) Pass such other or further orders, including incidental or consequential reliefs, as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the present case and in the interest of justice._ Order in Petition No. 130/MP/2026 Order in Petition No. 130/MP/2026 Order in Petition No. 130/MP/2026 _2. After considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the Petitioner, the Commission ordered as under:_ _(b) The Respondent to file its reply, if any, within three weeks, with a copy to the Petitioner, who may file its rejoinder within two weeks thereafter.”_ _“At the outset, the learned senior counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the present Petition has been filed seeking relaxation of Regulation 22(3)(c) of the Indian Electricity Grid Code (IEGC), 2023, for permitting the Petitioner to commission its Wind Power Project in a phased manner, in tranches of not less than 5 MW per phase, as and when such capacity becomes technically ready for commissioning. The learned senior counsel submitted that the Petitioner is in a position to commission approximately 21 MW of its 36 MW Wind Project, on or before 30.6.2026; however, unless the minimum capacity threshold for trial run and commissioning of wind generating stations prescribed under Regulation 22(3)(c) of the IEGC is relaxed, the Petitioner would not be able to commission even such 21 MW capacity. The learned senior counsel also submitted that the Respondent/CTUIL has not filed any reply in the matter and that the matter may be reserved for order. The learned senior counsel also sought liberty to file his brief note of submissions._ _3. After considering the submissions of the learned senior counsel for the Petitioner and the representative for the Respondent, CTUIL, the Commission permitted the Petitioner to file its note of submissions within a week._ 6. Petitioner CPTPL, vide Written Submissions dated 16.01.2026, has submitted as under: Order in Petition No. 130/MP/2026 All material facts stated are evidenced through annexed documents and are not disputed. The issue involved in the present Petition is limited to the consideration of relaxation of the applicable Regulations. As on date, CPTPL is in a position to commission 21 MW out of the total 36 MW of the Project and is ready. CPTPL is planning to obtain FTC and other approvals by 20th June 2026 to complete the trial run and sell the same on the Power Exchange. Order in Petition No. 130/MP/2026 7. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner and perused the facts available on record. Order in Petition No. 130/MP/2026 15. The main argument of the petitioner is that there was a delay in the issuance of the in-principle and final grant of Connectivity by the CTUIL. Let us peruse the in-principle grant issued to the Petitioner quoted as under: Order in Petition No. 130/MP/2026 Order in Petition No. 130/MP/2026 Order in Petition No. 130/MP/2026 As per the above, it can be noted that Petitioner’s application dated 20.7.2024 was discussed in Sep’24, Oct’25, Dec’24, and Feb’25 and was issued in-principle in May 2025. Order in Petition No. 130/MP/2026 20. We are unable to agree with the Petitioner’s argument that it would have completed the project in 7 months had it been issued the in-principle grant of connectivity in August 2024, when it could not complete the project in 18 months. Also, the Petitioner cannot claim that it must be given Connectivity for 7 months as per its requirement. We observe that connectivity can be granted only from the date the transmission system is available or is likely to be available. Accordingly, we do not agree with the Petitioner’s argument that it was a force majeure situation due to the delay in the grant of Connectivity. Order in Petition No. 130/MP/2026 23. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner. The trial run is an elaborate process defined in the Grid Code whereby the entity is required to furnish documents and test reports and to carry out real-time operation in coordination with the RLDC after giving due notice. The minimum capacity for a trial run is 50 MW, except for an entity under Regulation 4.1(e) of the GNA Regulations, which may conduct a trial run for the capacity of connectivity to enable such entity to achieve the trial run. An entity, while seeking connectivity, is fully aware that it must complete the trial run at full capacity together. 24. We note that the Petitioner delayed in commissioning the entire capacity. We do not find the instant case a fit case for us to exercise our power to relax to permit the Petitioner to conduct a trial run for a smaller capacity. Accordingly, the Petitioner's prayer to permit phase-wise commissioning of its 36 MW Wind Power Project is rejected.
